title: PRI Consolidates One-Party Dominance
note: Well-documented: PRI held every governorship and near-total congressional control through corporatist structures. Mario Vargas Llosa's 'perfect dictatorship' phrase confirmed.

title: Mexican Miracle Begins — Sustained GDP Growth
note: 6–7% average annual GDP growth during the stabilizing development era confirmed by multiple economic sources.

title: Bracero Program Expands Mexican Labor Migration to the US
note: Program originally launched 1942, expanded through early 1950s, ended 1964 — all correct.

title: Adolfo Ruiz Cortines Elected — Women Granted Full Voting Rights
note: Year-off by 1: Ruiz Cortines was elected in 1952 but women's federal voting rights were constitutionally enacted on October 17, 1953 (amendment to Articles 34 and 115). First federal election with women voting was July 1955. The event should be dated 1953.

title: Henriquista Movement Suppressed
note: The main Alameda crackdown/massacre was July 1952; ongoing suppression through 1953–1954 (party registration cancelled 1954) is accurate. 1953 as the year of sustained suppression is defensible.

title: Peso Devaluation and Stabilizing Development Policy
note: Devaluation from 8.65 to 12.50 pesos per dollar in April 1954 confirmed. Ortiz Mena's stabilizing development framework confirmed. Minor: Ortiz Mena became Finance Minister under López Mateos (1958), not immediately in 1954 — rate was stabilized by the Ruiz Cortines government first.

title: Television Broadcasting Expands Nationally
note: Telesistema Mexicano (Televisa predecessor) expanded through mid-1950s. Government content control confirmed.

title: National Polytechnic Institute Student Protests
note: IPN student unrest in the 1950s is documented in Mexican political history as precursor to 1968 movement.

title: Teachers' Union Strike Challenges PRI Labor Control
note: MRM founded 1956–1958, challenging SNTE. Arrests and co-optation confirmed.

title: Mexico City Earthquake
note: Magnitude stated as 7.9 but actual magnitude was 7.6–7.8 Mw. More critically, death toll 'at least two hundred' is materially wrong — confirmed sources report 54–160 deaths. Both the magnitude and death toll are substantially overstated.

title: Railroad Workers' Strike Crushed
note: Strike began June 1958, crushed March 1959 under López Mateos. Vallejo arrested and imprisoned. Description is accurate; the decisive crackdown was 1959 but the strike began 1958.

title: Adolfo López Mateos Elected President
note: Elected July 1958, took office December 1958. Center-left positioning and Cuba policy confirmed.

title: Mexico Refuses to Expel Cuba from the OAS
note: Mexico's non-intervention policy and refusal to sever ties with Cuba is well-documented.

title: Agrarian Reform Revived Under López Mateos
note: López Mateos distributed more land than any president since Cárdenas. 'Roughly thirty million acres' is within range of documented figures.

title: Population Reaches 35 Million
note: Minor discrepancy: 1960 census recorded ~36.72 million, not 35 million. The 35 million figure is a rounded approximation; not materially wrong enough to classify as FALSE.

title: Guerrilla Activity Emerges in Guerrero
note: Lucio Cabañas began organizing in Guerrero in the early 1960s; killed by security forces 1974. Dirty War disappearances confirmed.

title: Díaz Ordaz Becomes PRI Presidential Candidate
note: Díaz Ordaz was Interior Secretary and became PRI candidate in 1963 through the dedazo mechanism. Confirmed.

title: National Museum of Anthropology Opens
note: Inaugurated September 17, 1964 by President López Mateos. Location in Chapultepec Park and Aztec Sun Stone confirmed.

title: Maquiladora Program Established at the Border
note: Border Industrialization Program established May 20, 1965. Link to end of Bracero Program confirmed.

title: Chihuahua Guerrilla Attack on Military Barracks
note: Arturo Gámiz attack on Cuartel Madera, Chihuahua, September 23, 1965. Confirmed as opening act of Mexico's Dirty War era.

title: University Student Strikes Spread Across Mexico
note: Student protests at multiple universities in 1966 documented as precursor to 1968.

title: Tlatelolco Treaty — Latin American Nuclear-Free Zone
note: Signed February 14, 1967. García Robles confirmed as chief architect, won Nobel Peace Prize 1982 (shared with Alva Myrdal). First nuclear-weapons-free zone in a populated area confirmed.

title: Tlatelolco Massacre
note: October 2, 1968, ten days before Olympics. Official figures underreported; credible estimates range into hundreds. Confirmed.

title: 1968 Student Movement and Mexico City Olympics
note: Smith and Carlos Black Power salute confirmed. Olympics in Mexico City confirmed. Student movement scale and legacy confirmed.

title: Dirty War Intensifies After Tlatelolco
note: Systematic disappearances post-1968 confirmed by CNDH and human rights documentation.

title: Luis Echeverría Takes Office — Populist Rhetoric Returns
note: Took office December 1, 1970. Apertura democrática strategy and contradictions confirmed.

title: Corpus Christi Massacre — Halcones Attack Students
note: June 10, 1971 confirmed. Death toll 'at least twenty-five' is conservative and within the credible range (official: 11; credible estimates: up to 120). Paramilitary Halcones with government links confirmed.

title: Lucio Cabañas' Guerrilla Campaign Escalates in Guerrero
note: Partido de los Pobres confirmed. Cabañas killed in 1974 confirmed. Counter-insurgency abuses documented.

title: Echeverría Expands State Role in the Economy
note: State expansion and deficit spending leading to 1976 crisis is well-documented.

title: Liga Comunista 23 de Septiembre Founded
note: Founded 1973 (merged groups from 1972–1973). Bank robberies, kidnappings, and government destruction by late 1970s confirmed.

title: Dirty War Disappearances Peak
note: CNDH confirmed at least 275 enforced disappearances. Early-to-mid 1970s as peak period confirmed.

title: Eugenio Garza Sada Kidnapped and Killed
note: Year-off by 1: Garza Sada was killed on September 17, 1973, not 1974. Multiple sources confirm the 1973 date definitively.

title: Major Oil Discoveries in Chiapas and Tabasco
note: Large oil discoveries in southeastern Mexico confirmed in the early-to-mid 1970s. Cantarell discovery 1976; onshore Chiapas-Tabasco fields confirmed from mid-1970s.

title: International Women's Year Conference in Mexico City
note: First UN World Conference on Women, Mexico City, June 19 – July 2, 1975. 133 delegations confirmed.

title: Peso Crisis and IMF Bailout
note: 1976 devaluation from 12.5 to ~22 pesos per dollar confirmed. IMF austerity conditions confirmed.

title: López Portillo Takes Power — Oil Boom Era Begins
note: 'Manage abundance' quote and oil-backed borrowing spree confirmed.

title: Political Reform — Opposition Parties Gain Legal Recognition
note: LOPPE political reform 1977, Reyes Heroles as Interior Secretary, PCM legalized — confirmed.

title: Cantarell Oil Field Begins Major Production
note: Year-off by 2+: Cantarell production began June 1979, not 1977. Field was discovered 1976. Peak of ~2 million bpd came in the early 2000s, not 'within a few years' of 1977.

title: Population Reaches 67 Million — Urbanization Transforms Mexico
note: 1980 census recorded ~66.8 million; 67 million is accurate rounding. Urbanization majority and Mexico City scale confirmed.

title: Mexico Debt Crisis — Default Announcement Shocks Global Finance
note: Silva Herzog's August 12, 1982 announcement confirmed. Bank nationalization by López Portillo August 31, 1982 confirmed.

title: Miguel de la Madrid Elected — Technocratic Turn Begins
note: Elected July 1982, took office December 1, 1982. US-educated technocrats and market liberalization shift confirmed.

title: Austerity Program Shrinks Mexican Economy
note: GDP contraction under IMF conditions in 1983 confirmed.

title: PAN Electoral Victories Signal Opposition Growth
note: PAN municipal wins in northern cities in 1983 confirmed. Often contested through fraud is documented.

title: Cross-Border Drug Trade Expands Rapidly
note: Guadalajara Cartel under Félix Gallardo expanding cocaine transshipment in mid-1980s confirmed.

title: 1985 Mexico City Earthquakes — Civil Society Born
note: Minor discrepancy: first earthquake was 8.0–8.1 Mw (not definitively 8.1), second was ~7.5. Deaths '~10,000' is the commonly cited figure (range 5,000–45,000). Civil society catalyst narrative confirmed.

title: DEA Agent Kiki Camarena Murdered by Guadalajara Cartel
note: February 1985 kidnapping and murder confirmed. US border closure and diplomatic crisis confirmed.

title: Mexico Joins GATT — Trade Liberalization Begins
note: Mexico joined GATT in 1986 confirmed.

title: Oil Prices Collapse — Fiscal Crisis Deepens
note: Oil price collapse >50% in 1986 confirmed. Severe impact on Mexico's public finances confirmed.

title: Mexico Hosts FIFA World Cup
note: Mexico hosted, Argentina won, Maradona's Hand of God goal confirmed. Pablo Larios as Mexico goalkeeper confirmed.

title: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Breaks with the PRI — Democratic Current
note: Corriente Democrática and PRI split confirmed. Cárdenas was former governor of Michoacán, not just any PRI member.

title: Presidential Election Fraud — 'Se Cayó el Sistema'
note: System crash narrative and Salinas declared winner with ~50% confirmed. Widespread credible belief Cárdenas won confirmed.

title: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Forms the PRD
note: PRD founded May 5, 1989 (formally; coalition formed late 1988). Broad left coalition confirmed.

title: First PRI Governor Defeated — Baja California
note: Ruffo Appel won Baja California governorship 1989, first PRI gubernatorial loss. Salinas concession confirmed.

title: PEMEX Oil Workers' Union Boss Arrested
note: La Quina arrested January 10, 1989 in dawn army raid. PEMEX union control broken confirmed.
